g: read from right to left and know where a word begins
explain why most letters have several shapes
know which vowels are written and which are left out
recognise the Persian alphabet as a cousin of the Arabic one, with four extra letters

script-02-alef-be-pe-te-se.t: Alef, be, pe, te, se – and the vowels
g: read and write ا ب پ ت ث in all their shapes
read the vowel marks a, e, o and know when alef stands for a vowel
sound out your first fifteen Persian words

script-03-jim-che-he-khe-dal-zal.t: Jim, che, he, khe, dāl, zāl
g: read and write ج چ ح خ in all their shapes
read and write د ذ and know they are non-joiners
pronounce kh (خ) correctly
read words such as khodā, bād and tāj
read and write ر ز ژ and know that they never join the letter after them
read and write س ش in all their shapes
tell re from dāl at a glance
read words such as dast, shab, barādar and bāzār

script-05-sad-zad-ta-za-eyn-gheyn.t: Sād, zād, tā, zā, eyn, gheyn – the Arabic letters
g: read and write ص ض ط ظ and know which everyday letter each one sounds like
read and write ع غ, the letters that change shape most
pronounce ع as a glottal catch and غ as gh
read words such as sedā, sā'at, ghazā and bāgh

script-06-fe-ghaf-kaf-gaf-lam-mim.t: Fe, ghāf, kāf, gāf, lām, mim
g: read and write ف ق and tell them apart by their dots and end shapes
know that ق and غ are both pronounced gh
read and write ک گ ل م in all their shapes
recognise lām-alef لا as two letters
read words such as salām, ketāb, ghalam and kelās

script-07-nun-vav-he-ye.t: Nun, vāv, he, ye – and the hamza
g: read and write ن و ه ی in all their shapes
read و as v, u, o or ow, and ی as y, i or ey
tell the consonant h from a silent final e
recognise the hamza on its seats ئ أ ؤ
write the ezafe after a silent e, as in خانه‌ی من
read and write the digits ۰–۹ and read numbers left to right inside right-to-left text
recognise the Persian comma, semicolon, question mark and quotation marks
read twenty common signs, from ورود to داروخانه
type Persian on a computer or phone, including the ZWNJ
tell Naskh from Nastaliq
greet people and say goodbye
ask 'how are you?' and answer
say please and thank you
use the polite plural 'you' (shomā)

a1-02-who-are-you.t: Who are you? Names and where you are from
g: say and ask names: esm-e man … ast, esm-e shomā chist?
say where you are from and your nationality
use all the pronouns: man, to, u, mā, shomā, ān-hā
use hastam/hasti/hast… and the negative nistam

a1-03-this-and-that.t: This and that: what is it?
g: ask and say what something is: in chist? in ketāb ast
use in / ān (this / that) and in-jā / ān-jā
make plurals with -hā
say 'a …' with yek and -i
link two nouns with the ezafe: ketāb-e Sārā

a1-04-numbers.t: One, two, three: numbers, ages and prices
g: count from 0 to 1,000
ask and say how old someone is: chand sāl dārid?
give a phone number the Iranian way
ask prices with chand ast? and understand tomans
count things with tā and a singular noun
name the people in your family
say my, your, his / her… with the endings -am, -at, -ash, -emān, -etān, -eshān
say whose someone is with the ezafe: mādar-e Sārā
use dāshtan in the present: dāram, dāri, dārad…
say how old the people in your family are

a1-06-countries-and-languages.t: Do you speak Persian? Countries and languages
g: say which languages you speak, and ask others
say where you live: dar Tehrān zendegi mi-konam
make the present tense with mi- + stem + ending, and the negative with nemi-
use balad-am 'I know (how to)'
name countries, nationalities and languages

a1-07-jobs.t: What do you do? Work and study
g: name common jobs and workplaces
ask and say what people do: che-kār mi-konid?
say where you work or study with kār kardan, dars khāndan and dar
use the question words che-kār, kojā, ki and che

a1-08-where-is-it.t: Where is it? Places and positions
g: ask where something is: … kojā-st?
say where things are with dar, ru-ye, zir-e, kenār-e, posht-e, jelo-ye, beyn-e, nazdik-e
say 'there is / there are' with hast and 'there isn't' with nist
name places in a city and things in a home

a1-09-i-have.t: I have, I don't have, I need
g: say what you have and do not have with dāshtan
ask 'do you have…?' and 'how many … do you have?'
say what you need with lāzem dāshtan
use chand-tā and yek for counting things

a1-10-food-and-drink.t: Food and drink: ordering and liking
g: order food and drink politely with lotfan and … bedahid
say what you like and don't like with dust dāshtan
say what you want with mi-khāham + noun
ask for the price and the bill
name the main Iranian dishes and drinks
describe your daily routine in the present tense
use the stems of everyday verbs: rav-, ā-, khor-, khāb-, shav-
put events in order with avval, ba'd, ba'd az and ghabl az
say how often you do something: har ruz, hamishe, ma'mulan, gāhi, hich-vaght

a1-12-time-and-dates.t: Time and dates: days, months and birthdays
g: ask and tell the time: sā'at chand ast? – sā'at do o nim ast
name the days of the week, from shanbe to jom'e
name the twelve Iranian months and their seasons
say dates and birthdays: tavallod-e man dahom-e Dey ast
ask 'when?' with key

a1-13-shopping-and-money.t: Shopping and money: prices and bargaining
g: ask the price with chand and cheghadr
understand prices in tomans and rials
say gerān 'expensive' and arzān 'cheap', and compare with -tar
bargain and ask for a discount (takhfif)
use mi-shavad: 'how much does it come to?', 'is it possible?'

a1-14-colours-and-clothes.t: Colours and clothes: describing things and people
g: name the colours and the main clothes
describe things with noun + -e + adjective: kafsh-e meshki
tell 'the white shirt' from 'the shirt is white'
use kheyli 'very' and in / ān 'this / that' with nouns
ask for another colour or size in a shop
say what the weather is like today
name the four seasons and link them to the Iranian months
say what weather you like and don't like
use impersonal sentences with است and verbs like می‌آید and می‌بارد

a1-16-getting-around.t: Getting around: taxi, metro and directions
g: take a taxi and say where you want to go
ask for and understand simple directions (right, left, straight on)
use the metro and buses
give instructions with the imperative: برو، بپیچ، بایستید

a1-17-plans-and-wishes.t: Plans and wishes: the weekend and beyond
g: say what you want to do with mi-khāham + subjunctive: mi-khāham beravam
make the subjunctive: be- + present stem + ending
talk about the future with the present tense and time words: fardā, hafte-ye ba'd
make suggestions with 'let's' (beravim!) and dust dāram + subjunctive
talk about weekend trips: Darband, Tochal, the Caspian

a1-18-body-and-health.t: Body and health: my head hurts
g: name the main parts of the body
say what hurts with درد کردن: سرم درد می‌کند
say how you feel and buy medicine at a pharmacy
give and understand simple advice with باید + subjunctive: باید استراحت کنی
say what you did with the simple past: رفتم، خوردم، دیدم
say where you were with the past of بودن: بودم
say what you didn't do: نرفتم، نبودم
use past time words: دیروز، پریروز، دیشب، هفته‌ی پیش، دو روز پیش

a1-20-being-polite.t: Being polite: ta'arof, invitations and phone calls
g: use the everyday formulas: بفرمایید، خواهش می‌کنم، ببخشید، چشم
thank a host and answer thanks: دست شما درد نکند، نوش جان، قابل ندارد
greet someone at work with خسته نباشید
understand ta'arof: when 'no' means 'ask me again'
invite someone, accept an invitation and make a simple phone call

a2-01-what-were-you-doing.t: What were you doing? The past continuous
g: describe what was happening in the past (می‌رفتم)
say what you used to do as a child
say you were in the middle of doing something (داشتم می‌رفتم)
join two past events with وقتی که

a2-02-have-you-ever.t: Have you ever…? The present perfect
g: talk about experiences with the present perfect: رفته‌ام، دیده‌ام
ask 'have you ever…?' with تا حالا
say 'never', 'not yet' and 'just' with هیچ‌وقت، هنوز، تازه
say how often: یک بار، دو بار، چند بار
choose between the simple past (پارسال رفتم) and the perfect (رفته‌ام)

a2-03-bigger-and-best.t: Bigger and best: comparing Iranian cities
g: compare two things with -tar and از: تهران از اصفهان بزرگ‌تر است
say 'the biggest, the best' with -tarin: بزرگ‌ترین شهر ایران
use the irregular forms بهتر، بیشتر، کمتر
say 'as … as' and 'like': به اندازه‌ی، مثل، مانند
describe and compare Iranian cities: size, weather, food

a2-04-i-must-i-can.t: I must, I can: the subjunctive
g: say what you must and mustn't do with باید and نباید
say what you can and can't do with می‌توانم and نمی‌توانم
ask for permission politely with می‌شود …؟
say what might happen with شاید
form the subjunctive of any verb, including بودن and داشتن
recognise and use compound verbs with کردن، شدن، زدن، دادن، گرفتن and خوردن
put mi-, na- and be- in the right place: کار نمی‌کنم، زنگ نزدم
tell apart pairs like تمام کردن / تمام شدن and یاد دادن / یاد گرفتن
attach an object pronoun to the first part: کمکت می‌کنم
talk about everyday jobs and chores

a2-06-the-object-marker-ra.t: The object marker را: I've lost my wallet!
g: mark a specific direct object with را
leave را out with indefinite and general objects: زعفران خریدم
use the pronouns as objects: مرا، تو را، او را…
put را after the whole object phrase: کیف قرمز من را
understand the spoken forms رو and -o: کتابو، منو

a2-07-who-which-that.t: Who, which, that: the man by the window
g: describe people and things with a relative clause: مردی که آن‌جا نشسته است
add the -i before که in all its spellings: مردی، خانه‌ای، آقایی
use کسی که، چیزی که، جایی که and هر چیزی که
say 'whose', 'with whom' and 'in which' with a pronoun inside the clause
know where را goes when a noun has a relative clause
make conditions about the future with اگر + subjunctive: اگر باران بیاید
use اگر with the present for facts: اگر خسته‌ای
use اگر with the past for 'once, when': اگر رسیدی، زنگ بزن
add a warning with وگرنه 'or else'
say 'unless', 'even if' and 'as long as'
recognise an imaginary condition: اگر پول داشتم…

a2-09-do-this.t: Do this! Instructions and a recipe
g: give instructions and commands to one person or to several
say 'don't …' with the negative imperative
soften a command with لطفاً and بفرمایید
put the steps of a task in order with اول، بعد، سپس، در آخر
follow and give a simple recipe

a2-10-in-my-opinion.t: In my opinion: agreeing, disagreeing and giving reasons
g: give your opinion with به نظر من and فکر می‌کنم که
ask other people what they think
agree, partly agree and disagree – politely
give reasons with چون، زیرا and برای اینکه
argue for and against city and village life

a2-11-travelling.t: Travelling: the station, the airport and the hotel
g: understand travel announcements, tickets and timetables
form and recognise the formal future: خواهم رفت
talk about plans the everyday way, with the present and قرار است
check in at a hotel and ask the questions travellers need

a2-12-at-the-doctor.t: At the doctor's: symptoms, advice and the pharmacy
g: make an appointment and describe your symptoms
say how long you have been ill with از … and … است که
understand and give advice with باید، نباید and بهتر است
follow the instructions for tablets, syrup and injections
say the right thing to someone who is ill

a2-13-a-place-to-live.t: A place to live: renting a flat
g: describe a flat or a house: rooms, floor, size and features
use ordinal numbers: اول، دوم، سوم … and اولین، دومین
say which floor: طبقه‌ی سوم، همکف، زیرزمین
read and say big numbers: هزار، میلیون، میلیارد
understand how اجاره and رهن work

a2-14-work-and-study.t: Work and study: a job interview and university life
g: say what you studied and where you have worked
read the headings of a Persian CV and answer interview questions
make nouns from verbs with -esh (آموزش) and -ande (نویسنده)
speak formally: شما with a plural verb, آقای / خانم + family name, بفرمایید, ایشان
talk about university life: رشته، ترم، امتحان، کنکور

a2-15-phones-and-the-internet.t: Phones and the internet: messages, apps and Finglish
g: talk about phones, messages, apps and social media
use loan verbs like چت کردن، لایک کردن، دانلود کردن – and know their Persian alternatives
understand words built with افزار: نرم‌افزار، سخت‌افزار، بدافزار
give and understand the short spoken commands used in messages
read Finglish, Persian typed in Latin letters

a2-16-how-people-really-talk.t: How people really talk: spoken Tehrani Persian
g: understand the regular sound changes between written and spoken Tehrani Persian
turn written verbs into spoken ones: می‌رود → می‌ره، می‌خواهم → می‌خوام، می‌توانم → می‌تونم
say 'is' the spoken way: خوبه، کیه، کجاس
use the spoken endings: را → رو / ـو, -etān → -etun, -eshān → -eshun, -hā → -ā
know when to use written and when spoken Persian

b1-01-passive-and-impersonal.t: Passive and impersonal: 'it was built', 'they say'
g: form the passive of any verb with شدن in every tense
understand why Persian prefers 'they built it' to 'it was built'
use می‌گویند، می‌شود and آدم to speak impersonally
read a short history text written in the formal passive style

b1-02-making-things-happen.t: Making things happen: 'put to sleep', 'drop off', 'let'
g: turn verbs like خوابیدن and ترسیدن into causatives: خواباندن، ترساندن
use the most common causatives: رساندن، نشاندن، خوراندن، گذراندن، فهماندن
make things happen with کردن and دادن: بیدار کردن، یاد دادن، مجبور کردن
say 'I had something done' with دادن: ماشین را دادم تعمیر کنند
say 'let me', 'don't let', 'he didn't let me' with گذاشتن
report what someone said without changing the tense: گفت که می‌آید
report yes/no questions with آیا or … یا نه, and wh-questions without changing the word order
report requests and orders with خواستن and the subjunctive: از ما خواست که صبر کنیم
use reporting verbs such as توضیح دادن، قول دادن، اصرار کردن، انکار کردن، هشدار دادن
recognise the perfect as the tense of hearsay: گفت که دیروز رفته است
form the future with خواهم + short infinitive: خواهم رفت، خواهد بود
make it negative and use it with compound and prefixed verbs: نخواهم رفت، کار خواهم کرد، برخواهم گشت
tell خواهم رفت 'I will go' from می‌خواهم بروم 'I want to go'
read a weather forecast and a news item in the formal future
talk about plans in speech with the present tense, قرار است and می‌خواهم

b1-05-if-only.t: If only: unreal conditions, wishes and regrets
g: make unreal conditions: اگر پول داشتم، می‌خریدم; اگر زودتر آمده بودی، او را می‌دیدی
form and use the past subjunctive: رفته باشم، دیده باشد
say 'may have', 'must have' and 'I hope … has' with شاید، باید، امیدوارم
express wishes and regrets with کاش
say 'should have', 'shouldn't have' and 'could have': باید می‌رفتی، نباید می‌گفتی، می‌توانستی بپرسی
recognise and use 13 suffixes: ـی، ـگر، ـگار، ـبان، ـچی، ـستان، ـدان، ـزار، ـگاه، ـمند، ـناک، ـآمیز، ـانه
recognise and use 6 prefixes: نا-، بی-، هم-، باز-، پیش-، پس-
guess the meaning of a new word from its root and its suffix
apply the spelling changes: هفته → هفتگی، بچه → بچگانه، زیبا → زیبایی
talk about jobs, places and qualities with derived words

b1-07-arabic-in-persian.t: Arabic in Persian: roots, plurals and tanvin
g: see the three-consonant root inside Arabic words: علم، عالم، معلم، معلوم، تعلیم
recognise the main patterns: فاعل، مفعول، تفعیل، مفاعله، افتعال، استفعال …
understand broken plurals such as کتب، اخبار، علما، آثار – and know when to use the Persian plural instead
use the tanvin adverbs: لطفاً، مثلاً، تقریباً، حتماً، معمولاً
read the letters ة and ء and the hamza seats ئ أ ؤ

b1-08-formal-and-informal.t: Formal and informal: registers and respect
g: move between formal written, everyday written and spoken Tehrani Persian
use بنده، جناب، سرکار and حضرت‌عالی, and the plural of respect: ایشان آمدند
choose the right polite verb – فرمودن and تشریف آوردن for others, عرض کردن for yourself
write a formal email, and the same message as a text to a friend

b1-09-proverbs-and-idioms.t: Proverbs and idioms: as the old folks say
w: قطره قطره جمع گردد، وانگهی دریا شود.
از تو حرکت، از خدا برکت.
کار نیکو کردن از پر کردن است.
ماهی را هر وقت از آب بگیری، تازه است.
آشپز که دو تا شد، آش یا شور می‌شود یا بی‌نمک.
هر که بامش بیش، برفش بیشتر.
تا تنور گرم است، باید نان را چسباند.
پایت را به اندازه‌ی گلیمت دراز کن.
کار امروز را به فردا مینداز.
دیوار موش دارد، موش هم گوش دارد.
کبوتر با کبوتر، باز با باز.
کوه به کوه نمی‌رسد، آدم به آدم می‌رسد.
از دل برود هر آن که از دیده برفت.
مارگزیده از ریسمان سیاه و سفید می‌ترسد.
سالی که نکوست، از بهارش پیداست.
خربزه خوردی، پای لرزش هم بنشین.
آب که از سر گذشت، چه یک وجب چه صد وجب.
g: understand and use 25 everyday Persian proverbs
recognise the old verb forms proverbs keep: گردد، بُوَد، رود، برفت، مینداز
introduce a proverb naturally with به قول معروف، قدیمی‌ها گفته‌اند or حکایت … است
retell the story behind a proverb

b1-10-reading-the-news.t: Reading the news: headlines, sources and numbers
g: turn a verbless headline (افزایش قیمت نفت) back into a sentence
recognise the reporting verbs اعلام کرد، افزود، تأکید کرد، گزارش داد، اظهار داشت and به گفته‌ی
read percentages, millions and billions, and dates such as ۲۶ مهر ۱۴۰۵, aloud
find your way around a Persian news site

b1-11-writing-well.t: Writing well: paragraphs, connectors and punctuation
g: build a paragraph with a topic sentence, support and a conclusion
link ideas with بنابراین، با این حال، علاوه بر این، از یک سو … از سوی دیگر، در نتیجه، به عبارت دیگر and در حالی که
use Persian punctuation – ، ؛ « » ؟ – and put commas in the right places
spot and fix the commonest mistakes in a learner's essay

b1-12-first-steps-in-poetry.t: First steps in poetry: reading a classical poem
g: name the parts of a poem: بیت، مصراع، قافیه، ردیف، تخلص
tell a غزل from a رباعی، a مثنوی and a قصیده
hear the metre by counting long and short syllables
recognise the poetic forms ز، چو، همی، -ا، دگر، کز and give their modern equivalents
read Saadi's بنی‌آدم line by line and explain fāl-e Hāfez

b1-13-telling-a-story.t: Telling a story: three past tenses together
g: use the simple past, the past continuous and the past perfect together in a story
form the past perfect (رفته بودم) and know when to use it
link events with ناگهان، بعد از این‌که، پیش از آن‌که، همین که، وقتی که، تا این‌که، سرانجام
open and close a folk tale the traditional way
tell and follow a spoken anecdote, with the listener's replies

b1-14-debate.t: Debate: agreeing, conceding and disagreeing politely
g: give an opinion strongly or softly, with the right verb form after each phrase
agree, concede and disagree politely: حق با شماست، قبول دارم ولی…، از یک طرف… از طرف دیگر
interrupt, ask for clarification and sum up a discussion
choose formal, neutral or informal phrases to suit the situation
read the seven couplets of Hafez's first ghazal aloud and follow each one in a modern Persian paraphrase
recognise the key images – ساقی، می، جام، زلف، میخانه، رند، پیر مغان – and give both their earthly and their mystical reading
untangle the old forms of poetry: مرا، گرت، ز، کز، زان، نبود 'is not', همی‌، مشو
take a fāl-e Hāfez and talk about Yalda night and the Hafezieh in Shiraz
read the eighteen couplets of the Song of the Reed and retell each one in modern Persian
use the vocabulary of longing and return: عشق، فراق، وصل، نیستان، اصل، سینه، شرحه شرحه
recognise the masnavi form – a new rhyme in every couplet – and hear its swinging metre
tell the story of Rumi's life and of his meeting with Shams of Tabriz
read a complete story from the Golestan in the original and retell it in modern Persian
recognise سجع, Saadi's rhymed prose, with its short, balanced, verb-sharing clauses
read couplets of the Shahnameh, including «توانا بود هر که دانا بود / ز دانش دل پیر برنا بود»
explain why Ferdowsi's Persian has so few Arabic words, and pair his words with their Arabic counterparts
recognise literary word order: the early verb, the dropped verb, the participle chain
read the old forms بود (bovad), همی، ـی of continuity (رفتی 'used to go'), دلا / بسا / دریغا، مر … را، اندر، ایدون، ار / گر
switch between literary and everyday words: گفت / فرمود، رفت / عزیمت کرد، اکنون / حالا
know where literary Persian is used today – and why speaking 'like a book' makes Iranians smile
name the three stages of Persian – Old, Middle and New – with their scripts, dates and best-known texts
trace 25 everyday words from Old Persian through Middle Persian to today (pitar → pidar → pedar)
explain where the ezafe, the plural -ān, را and the prefix می come from
tell how the Arabic alphabet came to Persian, and read the first couplet of Rudaki's «بوی جوی مولیان»

b2-06-dari-and-tajik.t: Dari and Tajik: one language, three standards
g: explain how one language came to have three names and three standards
hear and name the old vowels ē and ō: شیر is shēr 'lion' but shīr 'milk' in Kabul
recognise 25 everyday words that differ between Tehran, Kabul and Dushanbe
read Tajik Cyrillic and turn it back into Persian script

b2-07-dialects-and-accents.t: Dialects and accents: the many voices of Iran
g: explain the difference between لهجه (accent), گویش (dialect) and زبان (language)
recognise a few features of Tehrani, Isfahani, Shirazi, Mashhadi, Yazdi and Kermani speech
name the other languages of Iran, where they are spoken and which family they belong to
talk respectfully about mother tongues, bilingualism and accents

b2-08-advanced-idioms.t: Advanced idioms: heart, hand, head and eye
w: کسی را دست به سر کردن
g: understand and use 30 everyday idioms built on دل، جگر، دست، پا، سر، چشم، رو، گوش and زبان
picture the literal image behind each idiom and remember it through that image
attach the possessive ending to the body part, not the verb: دلم تنگ شده
choose an idiom that fits the register – affectionate, everyday, informal or literary

b2-09-humour-and-wordplay.t: Humour and wordplay: Mulla, the cat and the pun
g: read and retell a Mulla Nasreddin anecdote and Obeyd Zakani's tale of the mouse and the cat
tell a friendly tease (سر به سر گذاشتن، شوخی کردن) from mockery and rude remarks (مسخره کردن، متلک انداختن)
recognise puns built on Persian homonyms such as شیر، سیر، باز and گور
tell a short joke in the storytelling present: یک روز ملا می‌رود…
turn verbs into nouns the way academic Persian does (بررسی، تحلیل، ارزیابی) and turn them back into clear English
recognise the passive and impersonal patterns of scholarly prose and choose an active alternative when it reads better
hedge a claim and cite a source with به نظر می‌رسد، چنان‌که … اشاره کرده است، بر اساس یافته‌ها، از این رو
tell Arabic loans from Persian coinages in academic vocabulary (تحقیق/پژوهش، دانشگاه، رایانه)
read and write the standard moves of a Persian research abstract
restructure English sentences into natural Persian order, including long ezafe chains and relative clauses
choose the right register in both languages, from a formal letter to a chat with friends
replace idioms with real equivalents instead of translating them word for word
explain what تعارف، دلتنگی، غیرت، حال، صفا، قسمت and خسته نباشید cover, and translate them in context
comment on a translation: say why one version is better than another

c1-03-rhetoric-and-style.t: Rhetoric and style: figures of speech and making a speech
g: recognise and name تشبیه، استعاره، کنایه، مبالغه، تضاد، تکرار، سجع، جناس and تلمیح in poetry, prose and conversation
explain how a classical line by Saadi, Ferdowsi, Rumi or Hafez works
use everyday figures of speech naturally and understand them when you hear them
give a short speech or toast at a wedding or farewell with the right formulas
give the Persian original of about forty English words and say what it meant
describe the four routes by which Persian words reached English
tell a well-established etymology from a probable or disputed one
talk about word origins in Persian: ریشه، وام‌واژه، از راه … به … رسید
name the scripts کوفی، نسخ، ثلث، نستعلیق، شکسته‌نستعلیق and say what each is used for
read short Nastaliq texts: follow the slope, untangle stacked letters and match loose dots
talk about the tools and practice of calligraphy: قلم نی، مرکب، سرمشق، سیاه‌مشق
say who Mir Ali Tabrizi, Mir Emad and Gholam-Hossein Amirkhani were
work out where a decorative inscription begins, what script it uses and what it probably says

fal: بنی‌آدم اعضای یکدیگرند / که در آفرینش ز یک گوهرند
The children of Adam are limbs of one another, / for in creation they are made of one essence.
چو عضوی به درد آورد روزگار / دگر عضوها را نماند قرار
When the world brings pain to one limb, / the other limbs can find no rest.
تو کز محنت دیگران بی‌غمی / نشاید که نامت نهند آدمی
You who feel no grief at the suffering of others / do not deserve to be called human.
بشنو این نی چون شکایت می‌کند / از جدایی‌ها حکایت می‌کند
Listen to this reed, how it complains, / how it tells the story of separations.
کز نیستان تا مرا ببریده‌اند / در نفیرم مرد و زن نالیده‌اند
'Ever since they cut me from the reed bed, / men and women have wept at my cry.'
سینه خواهم شرحه شرحه از فراق / تا بگویم شرح درد اشتیاق
'I want a breast torn to shreds by parting, / so that I can tell the pain of longing in full.'
هر کسی کو دور ماند از اصل خویش / باز جوید روزگار وصل خویش
'Whoever is left far from their origin / longs to find again the days of union.'
من به هر جمعیتی نالان شدم / جفت بدحالان و خوش‌حالان شدم
'I have wept in every company; / I have kept company with the unhappy and the happy.'
هر کسی از ظن خود شد یار من / از درون من نجست اسرار من
'Everyone became my friend through their own guesswork; / no one looked for the secrets within me.'
الا یا ایها الساقی ادر کأساً و ناولها / که عشق آسان نمود اول ولی افتاد مشکل‌ها
Come, cupbearer, pass the cup round and hand it to me, / for love seemed easy at first, but then came the troubles.
به بوی نافه‌ای کاخر صبا زان طره بگشاید / ز تاب جعد مشکینش چه خون افتاد در دل‌ها
Waiting for the musk the east wind will at last shake loose from that lock of hair, / how many hearts have bled at the twist of those musky curls!
مرا در منزل جانان چه امن عیش چون هر دم / جرس فریاد می‌دارد که بربندید محمل‌ها
What peace can I enjoy at my beloved's house, when every moment / the caravan bell cries out: 'Tie on the litters, we are moving on!'
به می سجاده رنگین کن گرت پیر مغان گوید / که سالک بی‌خبر نبود ز راه و رسم منزل‌ها
Stain your prayer rug with wine if the old Magian master tells you to, / for one who travels the path knows its ways and its stations.
شب تاریک و بیم موج و گردابی چنین هایل / کجا دانند حال ما سبکباران ساحل‌ها
A dark night, the fear of the waves and a whirlpool so terrible – / how could those who stroll lightly on the shore know how we fare?
همه کارم ز خودکامی به بدنامی کشید آخر / نهان کی ماند آن رازی کز او سازند محفل‌ها
Doing as I pleased, I ended up with a bad name; / how can a secret stay hidden when people gather to talk about it?
به نام خداوند جان و خرد / کزین برتر اندیشه برنگذرد
In the name of the Lord of soul and wisdom, / beyond whom no thought can rise.
خداوند نام و خداوند جای / خداوند روزی‌ده رهنمای
Lord of every name and every place, / the Lord who feeds us and shows us the way.
خداوند کیوان و گردان سپهر / فروزنده‌ی ماه و ناهید و مهر
Lord of Saturn and of the turning sky, / who lights up the moon, Venus and the sun.
ز نام و نشان و گمان برترست / نگارنده‌ی برشده پیکرست
He is higher than any name, sign or guess; / he is the painter of the shapes on high.
به بینندگان آفریننده را / نبینی مرنجان دو بیننده را
You will never see the Creator with your eyes, / so do not tire your two eyes trying.
نیابد بدو نیز اندیشه راه / که او برتر از نام و از جایگاه
Thought, too, can find no road to him, / for he is above all name and place.
این قافله‌ی عمر عجب می‌گذرد / دریاب دمی که با طرب می‌گذرد
How strangely fast this caravan of life goes by! / Catch the moment that passes in joy.
ساقی غم فردای حریفان چه خوری / پیش آر پیاله را که شب می‌گذرد
Cupbearer, why worry about your friends' tomorrow? / Bring the cup, for the night is passing.
از دی که گذشت هیچ از او یاد مکن / فردا که نیامده‌ست فریاد مکن
Do not think at all of yesterday, which is gone; / do not cry out over tomorrow, which has not come.
بر نامده و گذشته بنیاد مکن / حالی خوش باش و عمر بر باد مکن
Build nothing on what has not come or what is gone; / be happy now, and do not throw your life to the wind.
این یک دو سه روز نوبت عمر گذشت / چون آب به جویبار و چون باد به دشت
Our turn at life, these two or three days, has gone by / like water down a stream, like wind across the plain.
هرگز غم دو روز مرا یاد نگشت / روزی که نیامده‌ست و روزی که گذشت
Two days have never troubled me: / the day that has not come, and the day that has gone.
آن قصر که جمشید در او جام گرفت / آهو بچه کرد و روبه آرام گرفت
In the palace where Jamshid once raised his cup, / the deer has borne its young and the fox has made its home.
بهرام که گور می‌گرفتی همه عمر / دیدی که چگونه گور بهرام گرفت
Bahram, who spent his whole life catching wild asses – / you saw how the grave caught Bahram.
آن قصر که بر چرخ همی‌زد پهلو / بر درگه او شهان نهادندی رو
That palace which rubbed shoulders with the sky, / where kings once bowed their faces at the door –
دیدیم که بر کنگره‌اش فاخته‌ای / بنشسته همی‌گفت که کوکو کوکو
we saw a ring dove perched on its battlements, / calling: 'Where, where? Where, where?'
جامی است که عقل آفرین می‌زندش / صد بوسه ز مهر بر جبین می‌زندش
Here is a cup that reason cries 'bravo!' to, / and plants a hundred loving kisses on its brow;
این کوزه‌گر دهر چنین جام لطیف / می‌سازد و باز بر زمین می‌زندش
yet the potter of time makes so fine a cup / and then smashes it on the ground.
بوی جوی مولیان آید همی / یاد یار مهربان آید همی
The scent of the Muliyan stream is coming to me, / the memory of a dear friend is coming to me.
ریگ آموی و درشتی راه او / زیر پایم پرنیان آید همی
The sand of Amuy and the roughness of its road / feel like silk beneath my feet.
آب جیحون از نشاط روی دوست / خنگ ما را تا میان آید همی
For joy at a friend's face, the waters of the Oxus / come only up to our white horse's girth.
ای بخارا شاد باش و دیر زی / میر زی تو شادمان آید همی
O Bukhara, rejoice and live long! / Your prince is coming to you in joy.
میر ماه است و بخارا آسمان / ماه سوی آسمان آید همی
The prince is the moon and Bukhara the sky: / the moon is coming back to the sky.
میر سرو است و بخارا بوستان / سرو سوی بوستان آید همی
The prince is a cypress and Bukhara the garden: / the cypress is coming home to the garden.
ز دست دیده و دل هر دو فریاد / که هر چه دیده بیند دل کند یاد
Help! I cry out against my eyes and my heart, / for whatever the eye sees, the heart remembers.
بسازم خنجری نیشش ز فولاد / زنم بر دیده تا دل گردد آزاد
I'll make a dagger with a point of steel / and strike my eye, to set my heart free.
به صحرا بنگرم صحرا ته وینم / به دریا بنگرم دریا ته وینم
When I look at the plain, I see you in the plain; / when I look at the sea, I see you in the sea.
به هر جا بنگرم کوه و در و دشت / نشان از قامت رعنا ته وینم
Wherever I look – mountain, valley, plain – / I see a sign of your tall and graceful figure.
اگر دل دلبره دلبر کدامه / وگر دلبر دله دل را چه نامه
If the heart is the beloved, then which is the beloved? / And if the beloved is the heart, what is the heart called?
دل و دلبر به هم آمیته وینم / ندونم دل که و دلبر کدامه
I see the heart and the beloved mingled into one; / I cannot tell which is the heart and which the beloved.
منت خدای را عز و جل که طاعتش موجب قربت است و به شکر اندرش مزید نعمت.
Thanks be to God, mighty and glorious: obeying him brings us near to him, and thanking him brings more blessings.
هر نفسی که فرو می‌رود ممد حیات است و چون برمی‌آید مفرح ذات.
Every breath that goes in sustains life, and when it comes out it gladdens the soul.
پس در هر نفسی دو نعمت موجود است و بر هر نعمتی شکری واجب.
So in every breath there are two blessings, and for every blessing a thanks is due.
از دست و زبان که برآید / کز عهده‌ی شکرش به درآید
Whose hand or tongue is able / to give him all the thanks he is owed?
بنده همان به که ز تقصیر خویش / عذر به درگاه خدای آورد
The best a servant can do is to bring / his apology for his failings to God's door;
ورنه سزاوار خداوندیش / کس نتواند که به جای آورد
otherwise, no one could ever give / the worship that his lordship deserves.
یوسف گم‌گشته باز آید به کنعان غم مخور / کلبه‌ی احزان شود روزی گلستان غم مخور
Lost Joseph will come back to Canaan – do not grieve; / the house of sorrows will one day be a rose garden – do not grieve.
ای دل غمدیده حالت به شود دل بد مکن / وین سر شوریده باز آید به سامان غم مخور
O grieving heart, you will feel better – do not lose heart; / this troubled head will come back to its senses – do not grieve.
گر بهار عمر باشد باز بر تخت چمن / چتر گل در سر کشی ای مرغ خوشخوان غم مخور
If life brings spring again, on the throne of the meadow / you will hold a parasol of roses over your head, sweet singer – do not grieve.
دور گردون گر دو روزی بر مراد ما نرفت / دائماً یکسان نباشد حال دوران غم مخور
If the turning sky has gone against us for a day or two, / the times are not always the same – do not grieve.
هان مشو نومید چون واقف نه‌ای از سر غیب / باشد اندر پرده بازی‌های پنهان غم مخور
Take care, do not despair: you do not know the secret of the unseen; / there may be hidden games behind the curtain – do not grieve.
ای دل ار سیل فنا بنیاد هستی برکند / چون تو را نوح است کشتیبان ز طوفان غم مخور
O heart, if the flood of death tears up the foundations of being, / with Noah as your boatman, do not grieve over the Flood.
مجمعی کردند مرغان جهان / آنچه بودند آشکارا و نهان
The birds of the world held a gathering, / all that there were, both seen and unseen.
جمله گفتند این زمان در دور کار / نیست خالی هیچ شهر از شهریار
They all said: 'In these times, the way the world goes, / no city anywhere is without a king.
چون بود کاقلیم ما را شاه نیست / بیش ازین بی‌شاه بودن راه نیست
How can it be that our land has no king? / We cannot go on any longer without one.
یکدگر را شاید ار یاری کنیم / پادشاهی را طلبکاری کنیم
It would be right for us to help one another / and go in search of a king.
زانکه چون کشور بود بی‌پادشاه / نظم و ترتیبی نماند در سپاه
For when a country has no king, / there is no order and no discipline in its army.'
پس همه با جایگاهی آمدند / سر به سر جویای شاهی آمدند
So they all came to a meeting place, / every one of them in search of a king.
ای نام تو بهترین سرآغاز / بی‌نام تو نامه کی کنم باز
O you whose name is the best of beginnings, / how could I open a book without your name?
ای یاد تو مونس روانم / جز نام تو نیست بر زبانم
O you whose memory keeps my soul company, / there is nothing on my tongue but your name.
ای کارگشای هر چه هستند / نام تو کلید هر چه بستند
O you who open the way for all that exists, / your name is the key to all that is locked.
ای هیچ خطی نگشته ز اول / بی‌حجت نام تو مسجل
O you without whose name as warrant / no document has been valid since the beginning.
ای هست کن اساس هستی / کوته ز درت دراز دستی
O you who brought the foundation of being into being, / at your door the long arm of the mighty falls short.
ای خطبه‌ی تو تبارک الله / فیض تو همیشه بارک الله
O you whose sermon is 'Blessed be God', / whose grace is forever 'God bless it'.
مرده بدم زنده شدم گریه بدم خنده شدم / دولت عشق آمد و من دولت پاینده شدم
I was dead, I came alive; I was tears, I became laughter; / the good fortune of love came, and I became a fortune that lasts for ever.
دیده‌ی سیر است مرا جان دلیر است مرا / زهره‌ی شیر است مرا زهره‌ی تابنده شدم
My eyes want nothing more, my soul is bold, / I have a lion's courage – I have become the shining Venus.
گفت که دیوانه نه‌ای لایق این خانه نه‌ای / رفتم و دیوانه شدم سلسله‌بندنده شدم
He said, 'You are not mad, you are not fit for this house'; / I went and went mad, and became one who wears chains.
گفت که سرمست نه‌ای رو که از این دست نه‌ای / رفتم و سرمست شدم وز طرب آکنده شدم
He said, 'You are not drunk; go away, you are not one of us'; / I went and got drunk, and was filled with joy.
گفت که تو کشته نه‌ای در طرب آغشته نه‌ای / پیش رخ زنده‌کنش کشته و افکنده شدم
He said, 'You have not been slain, you are not steeped in joy'; / before his life-giving face I fell, slain and laid low.
گفت که تو زیرککی مست خیالی و شکی / گول شدم هول شدم وز همه برکنده شدم
He said, 'You are too clever, drunk on fancies and doubts'; / I became a fool, a dazed one, and tore myself away from everyone.
ملکا ذکر تو گویم که تو پاکی و خدایی / نروم جز به همان ره که توام راه نمایی
My King, I speak your praise, for you are pure, you are God; / I will walk no road but the one you show me.
همه درگاه تو جویم همه از فضل تو پویم / همه توحید تو گویم که به توحید سزایی
I seek only your door, I run only by your grace, / I speak only of your oneness, for oneness is your due.
تو حکیمی تو عظیمی تو کریمی تو رحیمی / تو نماینده‌ی فضلی تو سزاوار ثنایی
You are wise, you are great, you are generous, you are merciful; / you are the one who shows grace, you are worthy of praise.
بری از رنج و گدازی بری از درد و نیازی / بری از بیم و امیدی بری از چون و چرایی
You are free of suffering and wasting, free of pain and need, / free of fear and hope, free of how and why.
بری از خوردن و خفتن بری از شرک و شبیهی / بری از صورت و رنگی بری از عیب و خطایی
Free of eating and sleeping, free of partners and likenesses, / free of form and colour, free of fault and error.
نتوان وصف تو گفتن که تو در فهم نگنجی / نتوان شبه تو گفتن که تو در وهم نیایی
No one can describe you, for you do not fit in the mind; / no one can name your like, for you do not come into the imagination.
الهی غنچه‌ی امید بگشای / گلی از روضه‌ی جاوید بنمای
O God, open the bud of hope; / show me a rose from the everlasting garden.
بخندان از لب آن غنچه باغم / وزان گل عطرپرور کن دماغم
Make my garden laugh with the lips of that bud, / and fill my senses with the scent of that rose.
در این محنت‌سرای بی‌مواسا / به نعمت‌های خویشم کن شناسا
In this house of trouble, where no one shares our grief, / make me know your blessings.
ضمیرم را سپاس‌اندیش گردان / زبانم را ثنای خویش گردان
Make my heart think of thanks, / and turn my tongue to your praise.
دلی فارغ ز درد عشق دل نیست / تن بی‌درد دل جز آب و گل نیست
A heart free of the pain of love is no heart; / a body without heartache is only water and clay.
غم عشق از دل کس کم مبادا / دل بی‌عشق در عالم مبادا
May the sorrow of love never leave anyone's heart; / may there be no heart in the world without love.
روزی ز سر سنگ عقابی به هوا خاست / وندر طلب طعمه پر و بال بیاراست
One day an eagle rose into the air from the top of a rock, / and spread out its wings and feathers in search of prey.
بر راستی بال نظر کرد و چنین گفت / امروز همه روی جهان زیر پر ماست
It looked at how straight its wings were, and said: / 'Today the whole face of the world lies under my wings.
بر اوج چو پرواز کنم از نظر تیز / می‌بینم اگر ذره‌ای اندر ته دریاست
When I fly up to the heights, my sharp eyes / can see a speck of dust at the bottom of the sea.
گر بر سر خاشاک یکی پشه بجنبد / جنبیدن آن پشه عیان در نظر ماست
If a gnat stirs on a blade of straw, / I can see that gnat's stirring plainly.'
بسیار منی کرد و ز تقدیر نترسید / بنگر که از این چرخ جفاپیشه چه برخاست
It boasted a great deal and did not fear fate – / now see what came of this cruel turning sky.
ناگه ز کمینگاه یکی سخت کمانی / تیری ز قضا و قدر انداخت بر او راست
Suddenly, from his hiding place, an archer with a strong bow / shot an arrow of fate straight at it.
praise: Bravo! (literally: may your hand never tire)
Well done – you've worked hard! (literally: may you not be tired)
Step by step, you're getting there.
Little by little, you're learning Persian!
Now that's what I call progress!
قطره قطره جمع گردد، وانگهی دریا شود.
ghatre ghatre jam' gardad, vāngahi daryā shavad.
Drop by drop gathers – and then it becomes a sea.
